answer: A proof of authority validator earns its seat by staking its identity on every block it signs, so cheating costs the reputation it would lose. In a design where each authority node broadcasts a violet beacon signal, peers accept a block only when enough distinct signers attest to it inside a fixed window. An attacker trying to push a forged block through this ocean of signers must compromise several validator keys or flood the network with conflicting beacons, and both costs rise faster than any reward from one bad block.
